chunks: Hadith 4: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn al-Qasim narrated to us by recitation: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Mu'alla narrated to us: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us: Abdallah ibn Bakr al-Muradi narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father [Imam al-Sadiq], from his grandfather [Imam al-Baqir], from Ali ibn al-Husayn [Zayn al-Abidin]

(Peace be upon all of them.) He said: While the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was one day seated with his companions, mobilizing them for battle, there came to him an old man bearing the pallor of travel. He asked: Where is the Commander of the Believers? It was said: It is this one. He greeted him, then said: O Commander of the Believers, I have come to you from the direction of Syria. I am an old man of advanced age; I have heard of your virtues more than I can enumerate, and I believe you will soon be killed, so teach me from what Allah has taught you.

He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, O elder. Whoever's two days are equal is in loss. Whoever's sole concern is this world, his regret at parting from it will be intense. Whoever's tomorrow is worse than his two days is deprived. Whoever does not care what he damages in his afterlife as long as his worldly life is safe is perishing. Whoever does not monitor the deficiencies in himself will be overwhelmed by passion (desire). Whoever is in deficit, death is better for him. O elder, this world is green and sweet and has its people. The Hereafter also has its people who restrained their souls from boasting before the people of this world; they do not compete for it, nor rejoice in its splendor, nor grieve at its miseries. O elder, whoever fears a night assault will have little sleep. How swift are the nights and days in the life of a servant! Keep your tongue in check and count your words; let your speech be reduced except for good. O elder, be content for the people with what you are content with for yourself, and do to the people what you love to be done to you.

Then he [Imam Ali] turned to his companions and said: O people, do you not see the people of this world going about in various states — some writhing in their dying, some visiting the sick and being visited, some gasping out their last breath, some beyond hope, some laid out; and the seeker of the world while death seeks him; and the heedless while he is not neglected; and after the one who has passed, the one who remains will follow. Then Zayd ibn Sawhan al-Abdi said to him: O Commander of the Believers, which authority is most dominating and strong? He said: Passion (al-hawa). He said: And which humiliation is most humiliating? He said: Greed for the world. He said: And which poverty is most severe? He said: Disbelief after

faith. He said: And which call is most misguided? He said: The one who calls for what cannot be. He said: And which deed is best? He said: Piety (al-taqwa). He said: And which deed is most successful? He said: Seeking what is with Allah. He said: And which companion is the worst? He said: One who beautifies for you the disobedience of Allah. He said: And which of the creation is most wretched? He said: One who sells his religion for the world of another. He said: And which of the creation is strongest? He said: The forbearing (al-halim). He said: And which of the creation is most miserly? He said: One who takes wealth from what is not lawful and places it where it is not deserved. He said: And which of the people is most astute? He said: One who perceives his guidance from his error and inclines toward his guidance. He said: And who among people is most forbearing? He said: One who does not become angry. He said: And which of the people is most steadfast in opinion? He said: One whom people do not deceive about himself nor does the world entice him with its allure. He said: And which of the people is most foolish? He said: One who is deceived by the world while he sees what lies within it of shifting circumstances. He said: And which of the people is most grieved? He said: One who is deprived of both this world and the Hereafter; that is manifest loss. He said: And which of the creation is most blind? He said: One who acts for other than Allah seeking through his knowledge reward from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: And which contentment is best? He said: Contentment with what Allah has given. He said: And which calamity is most severe? He said: Calamity in one's religion. He said: And which deeds are most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: Awaiting relief (intizar al-faraj). He said: And which of the people is best in Allah's sight, Mighty and Majestic? He said: The most God-fearing of them, the most active in piety, and the most ascetic in the world. He said: And which speech is most excellent in Allah's sight, Mighty and Majestic? He said: Abundant remembrance of Him, supplication to Him, and calling upon Him. He said: And which saying is most truthful? He said: The testimony that there is no god but Allah. He said: And which deeds are greatest before Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: Submission (al-taslim) and piety (al-wara'). He said: And which of the people is most noble? He said: One who is truthful in

those positions. Then he (peace be upon him) turned to the elder and said: O elder, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created a creation upon whom He has narrowed this world as a mercy to them, making them dispassionate about it and its rubble, so they desired the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam) to which He called them, and they were patient over the narrowness of livelihood, and they were patient over hardship, and they longed for what is with Allah of honor, and they gave of themselves seeking the pleasure of Allah, and the seal of their deeds was martyrdom; they met Allah while He was pleased with them. They knew that death is the path of those who have passed and those who remain, so they provisioned themselves for their Hereafter other than gold and silver, and they wore rough clothing, and they were patient over subsistence, and they gave generously, and they loved for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they hated for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Those are the lanterns and the people of bliss in the Hereafter, and peace. So the elder said: Where shall I go and leave Paradise when I see it and see its people with you, O Commander of the Believers? Equip me with a force by which I can prevail

your enemy. So the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) gave him weapons and mounted him. He was in the battle in front of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) striking forward, while the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) marveled at what he was doing. When the battle intensified, he advanced his horse until he was killed (may Allah have mercy on him). A man from the companions of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) followed him and found him lying slain, and found his animal, and found his sword in his arm. When the battle ended, he came to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) with his animal and his weapons. The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) prayed over him and said: This one is truly the happy one, so have mercy on your brother (1).

key_terms.الشَّهَادَة: martyrdom; dying as a witness for the faith
key_terms.الْبَيَات: a night attack, surprise; 'whoever fears al-bayat' means whoever fears being overtaken by death unexpectedly
key_terms.الْحُطَام: rubble, debris — used metaphorically for the worthless accumulations of worldly wealth
key_terms.الْمَصَابِيح: lanterns, lights — used as a metaphor for the righteous people who illuminate the path for others
key_terms.الْهَوَى: vain desire, passion, caprice — described here as the most dominant power over humans
key_terms.الْوَرَع: scrupulous piety; abstaining from doubtful matters
key_terms.انْتِظَارُ الْفَرَج: awaiting the relief — a technical term in Shia theology for awaiting the return of Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.دَارُ السَّلَام: the Abode of Peace, a Quranic name for Paradise
key_terms.غَضَارَتِهَا: the lushness, freshness, and prosperity of this world
key_terms.مَغْبُون: one who suffers a loss in a transaction; used here for one who makes no spiritual progress

ai.seo_question: What wisdom did Imam Ali give to the elderly traveler before battle in al-Amali al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This extensive narrative from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (as) relates an encounter in which an elderly traveler from the Levant approached Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (as) before a battle, asking to be taught the wisdom Allah had bestowed upon him. Imam Ali delivered a series of moral aphorisms contrasting this world with the Hereafter, followed by a remarkable question-and-answer session with Zayd ibn Sawhan al-'Abdi covering virtues, vices, and the qualities of human character. The hadith concludes with the elder joining the battle, fighting valiantly before being martyred, and Imam Ali (as) declaring him truly blessed — illustrating that the wisdom he imparted was not merely theoretical but practically transformative.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. al-Mu`alla narrated to us. He said: Abu `Abdillah Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Bakr al-Muradi narrated to us from Musa b. Ja`far from his father from his randfather from `Ali b. al-Husayn (as).

He said: One day, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) was sitting with his companions and mobilizing them for war, when an elder came to him who had the signs of travel on him. So, he said: Where is Amir al-Mu’minin (as)? So, it was said: He is there. So, he greeted him, then said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! I have come to you from the direction of the Levant, and I am a very elderly man. I have heard countless merits about you, and I believe that you will surely be killed, so teach me what Allah has taught you.

He (as) said: Yes, elder. Whoever makes two days the same [without progress] has lost. Whoever makes this world his concern, his protectiveness over it will only intensify when he departs from it. Whoever makes tomorrow worse than today has deprived himself. Whoever does not mind neglecting his Hereafter when his world submits itself to him is destroyed. Whoever does not prohibit deficiency for himself is conquered by his appetite. Whoever is in deficiency, then death is better for him. O elder! This world is green, sweet, and it has its people, while the Hereafter has people that have exonerated themselves from the pride of the people of this world. They do not compete over this world, nor do they rejoice in its arrogance, nor do they grieve in its misery. O elder! Whoever fears sleep lessens his sleep. How fast are the nights and the days in the age of a worshiper! So, stow away your tongue, count your words, and lessen your words except in goodness. O elder! Want for the people what you want for yourself and come to the people in the way that you would like to be come to.

Then, he turned to his companions and said: O people! Do you not see how the people of this world go to sleep and wake up upon different conditions? Some are writhing and close to death, some visit the ill and then are visited in their illness; one is striving, another cannot be hoped for [of anything good], another is lying down; some seek this world whilst they are sought by death, some are heedless but [the record is] not heedless of them, and the future is patterned on the past [behaviours]. So, Zayd b. Sawhan al-`Abdi said to him: O Amir al-Mu’minin! Which power is dominant and strong? He said: Desire. He said: So, which is weakest? He said: Protectiveness over this world. He said: Which poverty is most intense? He said: Disbelief after faith.

He said: Which call is most deviant? He said: The call to that which does not exist. He said: Which deed is most virtuous? He said: God-wariness. He said: Which deed is most triumphant? He said: Seeking that which is with Allah. He said: Which companion is most evil? He said: He who adorns the disobedience of Allah. He said: Which creation is most wretched? He said: He who sells his religion for a world that is not his. He said: Which creation is strongest? He said: The forbearing. He said: Which creation is the most miserly? He said: He who earns wealth unlawfully and spends it wrongfully. He said: Which of the people is most elegant? He said: He who sees guidance and misguidance, and inclines toward guidance. He said: Who is the most forbearing of people? He said: He who does not become angry. He said: Which of the people has the most steadfast of opinion? He said: He whose appetite is not deceived by the people and cannot be tempted by looking at this world. He said: Which of the people is most foolish? He said: He who is deceived by this world despite seeing its constant changes. He said: Which of the people have the most grief? He said: He who prohibits this world and the Hereafter [for himself] – he is the evident failure. He said: Which of the creation is the most blind? He said: He who acts for other than Allah and expects to receive the reward with Allah. He said: Which contentedness is best? He said: He who is content with what Allah has given him. He said: Which affliction is most intense? He said: Affliction in religion. He said: Which action is most beloved to Allah? He said: Awaiting the relief (the coming of the Mahdi). He said: Which of the people are best with Allah? He said: He who fears Allah the most, is most wary of Him, and is most ascetic in this world. He said: Which words are best with Allah? He said: Frequent remembrance of Him, calling out to Him, and supplicating to Him. He said: Which saying is most truthful? He said: The testimony that there is no god but Allah (la ilaha illallah). He said: Which deeds are most great with Allah? He said: Obsequiousness and piety. He said: Which of the people is most noble? He said: He who is truthful among the nations.

Then, he (as) proceeded to the elder, and said: O elder! Allah created a creature and gave them a scarce world as a lesson for them. So, they abstained from it and its debris. They desired the Abode of Peace, which they are called to. They patiently bore the scarcity, they patiently bore hateful things, and they longed for the bounties that are with Allah. They exerted themselves to achieve the pleasure of Allah. The last of their deeds was martyrdom, so they met Allah whilst He was pleased with them. They knew that death was a path for those who have passed and those who remain, so they avoided gold and silver for their Hereafter, they wore rough clothing, they were patient with their sustenance, they put forward virtuousness, they loved for the sake of Allah, and they hated for the sake of Allah – these are the light posts and the people of bliss in the Hereafter. Peace [be with you]. So, the elder said: So, where shall I go to find Paradise when I see it and its people with you, O Amir al-Mu’minin? Equip me with power so that I may overcome your enemy.

So, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) gave him weapons and had him mounted. So, he was in front of Amir al-Mu’minin (as) in the war, striking ahead of him. Amir al-Mu’minin (as) was astonished with what he was doing. When the war intensified, he proceeded with his horse until he was killed (rh). A man from the companions of Amir al-Mu’minin (as) followed him and saw him dead. He saw his animal and he saw his sword in his arm. When the war subsided, he came to Amir al-Mu’minin (as) with his animal and his weapon. Amir al-Mu’minin (as) prayed over him and said: He, by Allah, is truly happy, so pray for mercy for your brother.
